At the same time, I have an intense, panicky fear of gaining weight, and even thinking about eating bread or rice makes me picture my face and stomach puffing out overnight.\n\nDoctor: When you look at your body, do you feel you are actually underweight or too thin, or do you mostly feel your weight is fine but are very afraid of gaining weight?\n\nPatient: Like I said, I don't see myself as underweight at all—I just see a lean, wiry frame that feels strong. My real issue is the thought of gaining weight, which absolutely panics me because I'm terrified of waking up looking bloated and puffy.\n\nDoctor: Do you restrict food mainly because you want to lose weight or stay thin, or is it more because eating certain foods makes you feel physically panicky or afraid of bloating and puffiness?\n\nPatient: It is definitely the latter. I mostly avoid eating more because the thought of gaining weight or getting puffy triggers a tight, panicky feeling in my chest.\n\nDoctor: When you look in the mirror, do you feel you are too thin or need to gain weight, or do you feel your weight is fine and mainly avoid eating because you fear gaining weight?\n\nPatient: When I look in the mirror, I don't see myself as too thin at all—I just see a lean, wiry strength and feel that others are overreacting. I really think my doctor and sister are overreacting when they call me \"frail\" and worry about my size.\n\nDoctor: Have your periods become irregular or stopped altogether since the weight loss?\n\nPatient: I actually went through menopause years ago since I'm 59, so I haven't had a period in a very long time. I feel like everyone else is overreacting, and I absolutely do not want to gain weight because the thought of eating more and looking puffy makes me feel completely panicky.\n\nDoctor: When you look at your body, do you believe you are actually too thin or underweight, or do you feel your current weight is fine and mainly fear gaining weight?\n\nPatient: When I look in the mirror, I honestly don't see myself as too thin or underweight; I just see a lean, wiry strength, and I think everyone else is overreacting. At the same time, I have an intense, panicky fear of gaining weight, and even thinking about eating bread or rice makes me picture my face and stomach puffing out overnight.\n\nDoctor: When you look at your body, do you feel you are actually underweight or too thin, or do you mostly feel your weight is fine but are very afraid of gaining weight?\n\nPatient: Like I said, I don't see myself as underweight at all—I just see a lean, wiry frame that feels strong. My real issue is the thought of gaining weight, which absolutely panics me because I'm terrified of waking up looking bloated and puffy.\n\nDoctor: Do you restrict food mainly because you want to lose weight or stay thin, or is it more because eating certain foods makes you feel physically panicky or afraid of bloating and puffiness?\n\nPatient: It is definitely the latter. Just thinking about eating foods like rice or bread gives me a tight, panicky feeling in my chest because I worry my stomach and face will puff up overnight. I would much rather go to bed hungry than face that kind of anxiety.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe you are actually underweight or too thin, or do you mainly feel your current weight is fine and avoid food because you fear gaining weight?\n\nPatient: I really don't think I'm underweight or too thin; to me, my current weight is just fine and I feel lean and strong, even if others are overreacting. But I definitely avoid certain foods because the thought of gaining weight and feeling puffy makes me feel incredibly panicky and anxious.\n\nDoctor: Have you lost weight because you believe you are too heavy or want to be thinner, or do you think your current weight is fine and mainly avoid eating because you fear gaining weight?\n\nPatient: I never thought I was too heavy, and I actually think my current weight is fine—it feels like a quiet victory to be this lean and wiry.
